scope: Independent static review of incomplete group-cache physical-retirement v2 experiment
reconstruction: V10 native manifest preimages match all three existing source files
Gzip expands to exact patch; standalone and v1-plus-delta forward/reverse source reconstruction match exactly
All six prior group test bodies and the entire original mock test file remain byte-identical prefixes
result: Not adoptable: prior provisional, speculative and uncached-fallback ownership blockers remain, and no native qualification exists.
positive_scope: Cached owner is retained across timeout and stream-lock waits; physical retirement replaces ConnIo under its stream lock.
Close now propagates a Timeout if it cannot acquire and retire the cached group slot within its deadline, and a bounded deferred task arranges later cleanup after close cancellation or timeout.
Linux fd tests inspect the exact socket inode rather than treating peer EOF as local fd destruction; procfs enumeration ignores only NotFound and fails closed on other errors.
The held-stream-lock control registers cleanup while the descriptor remains open, then releases the lock and checks eventual descriptor absence.

findings.detail: The expired_cached_fd_is_gone_before_a_replacement_is_accepted test checks inode absence only after listener.accept and after reading the replacement request. It cannot prove the fd was absent at the time of accept; the code does order physical retirement before discovery, but a pre-dial observation/gate is needed for that precise runtime claim.

Bootstrap and target negotiation, FindCoordinator, speculative rediscovery and busy fallback sockets remain in local futures without durable ownership. Close may report success while a parked uncached fallback retains an fd. Normal cancellation with a busy transport keeps a marked socket in the cache until another access or close.

limitations: All new Linux procfs controls are unrun and require accessible procfs; no type-check, Clippy, Cargo, live Kafka, TLS/SASL, non-Linux runtime or benchmark.
A deferred task needs the originating runtime to progress and the current lock owner to release; cancellation or timeout does not itself prove completion.
Metadata-v3 changes overlap and were not merged or independently checked as a composite.
Existing broader producer close-cancellation/worker lifecycle issue remains outside this experiment.
